title: The tech's year
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The tech's tally: sixty-five and the gap. He says the machine did two thousand six hundred sheets of Wood's this year. Wood says he didn't ask. The tech says nobody asks; that's why he counts. The strip draws the number as blocks. It knows it; it won't letter it.

panels.composition: The print shop, the term over, the TECH at the wall's tally. WOOD in the coat. BARNABY.

image.prompt: a print technician standing at a wall of pencil tallies in a quiet print shop while a young man in a chore coat and a small dog wait, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The tally: sixty-five, the gap. Under it, a number in the tech's hand, as blocks.

image.prompt: close on a wall with pencil tallies and a number written beneath them rendered as blocks, black and white, no words
image.notes: 2,600 sheets: as blocks. The strip knows; it won't letter it.

balloons.text: Two thousand six hundred of yours.
Nobody asks. That's why I count.

image.prompt: a print technician, dry, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The machine, off, for the holiday. The two of them and the dog. The number on the wall in blocks. Counting's not keeping; the tech counts anyway. Both are the strip's.

image.prompt: a large idle copier with two men and a small dog beside it and a wall of pencil tallies, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen over rough blue pencil; xerox grain; stark spotting; rain in frantic vertical hatching (Arc 1's aesthetic)

notes: 'Nobody asks. That's why I count.' The number, as blocks.
